content.text: All preferred elements are satisfied across §§ 13.2, 14.1–14.4. No redline needed.

input.quote: 14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.
input.rationale: The IP package meets our preferred position in full. § 14.2 gives us ownership of each Deliverable created specifically for us upon creation, with an express present assignment of all worldwide right, title and interest (plus personnel assignments and further-assurance cooperation). § 14.3 confirms Vendor retains only Vendor Technology (defined in § 1.8 as its pre-existing software, tools, models and templates, expressly excluding Customer Data and our pre-existing IP), and channels any embedded Vendor Technology into the § 13.2 licence, which is perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free and fully paid, and permits use, modification, derivative works and contractor support for our business — so the fallback deliverable-licence elements are exceeded as well. § 14.1 confirms we own all Customer Data and Customer-provided material and that no right transfers to Vendor except a limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support and improve the Services for Customer; that is service delivery for us, not independent exploitation, and § 15.1 reinforces it by barring sale, advertising use, cross-customer combination and model training absent our express written consent (a consent gate, not a standing licence). § 14.4 forecloses joint ownership unless the parties sign a separate instrument that identifies the IP and each party's exploitation rights, and preserves our unrestricted right to use our own feedback. The only sub-preferred details are that Deliverable ownership in § 14.2 is "subject to payment of the applicable Fees" and § 1.4 excludes unaided-memory know-how from Deliverables — both customary and noted for information only, not material deviations. No redline proposed.
